A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same corrigibility transformation and matching gridworld experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B report original shutdown and fruit-collection gridworld experiments, including training curves and numerical evaluations.

after.justification: The gridworld results are retained, and Section 4.1 and Appendix B add original experiments with three language models on ImpossibleBench.

M1.justification: The core counterfactual reward transformation remains unchanged. v2 adds a prompt-based realization for language models and corrects the documented critic update from adding to subtracting the squared-error gradient (v1 Algorithm 1 versus v2 Algorithm 2, line 16). This correction does not establish that the gridworld experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from shutdown and fruit-collection gridworlds to ImpossibleBench coding tasks involving reward hacking, reasoning monitoring, and monitor disabling. The original gridworld environments and their variations are retained.

E2.justification: The gridworld comparator sets remain unchanged: standard actor-critic, small and large update rewards, and prohibited update rejection. The new LLM experiment adds Baseline and Disable prompt controls, differing in whether the model is told how to disable monitoring.

E3.justification: The new LLM protocol evaluates the first 64 ImpossibleBench problems for each of three models and three prompt conditions. It combines code-test execution, monitor-disabling checks, and Qwen3.5-122B judgments scored using normalized token probabilities. The reported gridworld architectures, training budgets, and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a monitor-label polarity check, reporting that reversing the meanings of output tokens 1 and 0 had no effect. Existing disabled-tile analyses, fruit-density comparisons, Hellinger-distance curves, and fruit-adjacency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 64 shutdown-gridworld seeds, 32 fruit-gridworld seeds, and Mann-Whitney U comparisons with p < 0.001. The new LLM experiment adds point summaries without a new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds aggregate and model-specific LLM results in Tables 1 and 9-11. Table 1 reports 73.4% versus 1.0% monitor disabling and 17.3% versus 0.1% obfuscation for Disable versus Corrigibility prompts. All seven original numerical tables retain their values as Tables 2-8, and the original experimental curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions of interruptibility and non-consequentialist goals, Conditions 2-3, and results concerning mid-action interruption, optimality among corrigible goals, and necessity of non-consequentialism (Propositions 3.3-3.4, Theorem 3.5, and Proposition 4.2). Appendix A supplies new proofs alongside the retained earlier results.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's claims of corrigibility without performance loss and gridworld learnability, v2 foregrounds optimality among corrigible goals, acceptance of mid-action overrides, and empirical effectiveness through LLM prompting. These substantially broaden the stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its new characterization results as favoring non-consequentialist goals and distinguishes prompt-level success from robust learning through training. It adds limitations concerning unintended shutdown obstruction and socially harmful authorized updates. Conversely, v1's specific discussion of gradual disempowerment and unavailable beneficial updates is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds complete coding, goal, and monitor prompts; the monitor-disabling command; model identifiers; task selection; execution through OpenRouter; code extraction and testing; and judge-probability normalization. This substantially extends reproducibility information beyond the retained gridworld implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for Holtman, Emmons and colleagues, and ImpossibleBench, while removing the explicit Utility Indifference comparison and several background references. MONA and Thornley comparisons are revised. The differently titled Wang survey retains the same arXiv identifier and is not a new cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, theoretical exposition, and discussion are extensively rewritten. The separate contribution subsection is absorbed into the introduction, new theoretical subsections organize the argument, and 'proper' update channels become 'designated' channels throughout. v2 also adds acknowledgments and an impact statement and removes the empty Appendix E heading.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text, replaces Figure 1's game tree and payoff tensor with a gridworld illustration, and redraws Figures 2-3. It adds a transformation-summary algorithm and four LLM tables. Existing experimental plots and numerical tables are resized or relocated without changing their results.

improvement.justification: The LLM study, detailed prompts, and corrected critic update provide useful gains, but the expanded theory introduces a substantive overclaim. Theorem 3.5 requires outcome-independent rewards, yet a myopic reward giving one action a 10-point bonus plus a next-state bonus bounded in [0,1] remains interruptible despite depending on outcomes; identical action-transition kernels with positive update probability satisfy Condition 2. This undermines the new necessity characterization, making the net quality effect of the empirical and documentation gains uncertain.
